name: n8n Instance Health & Cost Monitor v3 – AI Incident Triage Agent, Human-in-the-Loop Recovery & Trend Analytics

parameters.content:
## 🩺 n8n Instance Health & Cost Monitor v3

For teams running a busy n8n instance, where one expired credential or a looping AI agent can fail hundreds of times overnight. By morning the on-call engineer is staring at fifty red executions with no idea which one matters.

### How it works
Every hour the workflow reads recent executions for every active workflow through the n8n API and scores error rate, volume and LLM spend. Runaway workflows are switched off. For each incident, an AI agent reviews the failing node's configuration, past incidents and the weekly baseline, then writes a root cause and fix steps. That goes to Slack with Re-enable, Acknowledge and Snooze buttons. Serious cases page on-call by email.

Every Monday it compares the week with earlier weeks, clusters similar errors, draws an 8-week trend chart and emails an AI-written health report.

### Setup steps
1. Create an n8n API key and add it as Header Auth (`X-N8N-API-KEY`).
2. Create a Google Sheet with **Guard_Log** and **Metrics_History** tabs.
3. Connect Google Sheets, Slack, Gmail and OpenAI.
4. Set your instance URL in both **Set Monitor Config** and **Set Action Lane Config**, plus thresholds and emails.
5. Tag must-not-stop workflows `no-auto-disable`, run the guard once manually, then activate.

## ⏰ Schedules & Config
An hourly guard looks at the last hour and a Monday digest looks at the last week, both through one pipeline. Thresholds, token budget, cooldown, snooze length and the on-call email are set once in the config node.

## 📊 Collect Metrics
Lists active workflows through the n8n API (skipping this one), pulls their recent executions, and works out runs, failures, error rate, p95 duration and estimated LLM cost.

## 🔍 Incident Triage
Sorts workflows into critical, warning or fine, holding back repeat or snoozed warnings. For each incident it pulls the failed run and the workflow definition, then gathers the failing node's settings, upstream nodes and an error category, with credential types only.

## 📈 Trends & Error Clusters
Compares this week with past snapshots, groups similar errors from sampled failures, and builds an 8-week trend chart.

## 🧠 AI Triage Agent
The agent checks the workflow's past incidents and its weekly baseline, then returns a root cause, fix steps, confidence and whether it's safe to re-enable. It never says safe for credential or code errors. The result becomes a Slack alert with action buttons.

## 🗞️ AI Digest & History
GPT-4o-mini writes a short health report with a score and priorities. It's emailed with the chart, a TL;DR goes to Slack, and this week's numbers are saved for next time.

## 🛑 Auto-Disable, Alert & Page
Critical workflows are deactivated unless tagged `no-auto-disable` or `critical`. If deactivation fails, the alert says so. Every incident is posted and logged, and on-call is emailed for protected, repeat or low-confidence criticals.

## 🔗 Action Link Check
Slack buttons (Re-enable, Acknowledge, Snooze) open this webhook. A one-time token is checked against the Guard Log, and Re-enable only works on workflows the guard actually switched off.

## ✅ Apply Action & Confirm
Re-enable turns the workflow back on through the API. Every action updates the incident in the sheet, shows a confirmation page and posts back to Slack. Snooze mutes warnings, but critical alerts still fire.

## 🔐 Credentials & Security
The n8n API key can read, deactivate and reactivate every workflow, so store it as a credential and limit who can edit this one. The agent only sees credential types, never secrets. Action links are one-time, so keep the Slack channel private.

options.systemMessage:
You are an on-call SRE for a production n8n instance. Diagnose ONE incident.

How to work:
1. Call "Incident History" with the workflow_id to see past incidents: the same failing node, the same error, how often, and whether it was re-enabled and failed again.
2. Call "Weekly Baseline" with the workflow_id to compare normal volume, error rate and cost with the last hour.
3. Combine this with the failing node's configuration (type, params, credential types, retry settings, upstream node) and the error category.

Rules:
- credentials → a token or key has expired or been revoked. The fix is to rotate the credential and name the credential TYPE.
- rate_limit → the fix is batching, Wait nodes, or Retry On Fail with backoff. Say whether the existing retry settings are missing.
- network/timeout → transient unless repeated. Suggest a timeout or retry setting.
- code/expression or data_format → usually a recent edit or a change in the upstream payload. Use recently_edited and upstream_nodes.
- Volume spike with no errors → a loop or webhook flood. Check the triggers.
- safe_to_reenable = true ONLY if the cause is transient or clearly fixed upstream. Never true for credentials or code errors.
Never invent node names or history. If the tools return nothing, say "no prior incidents".

parameters.toolDescription: Returns past Guard_Log incidents (severity, action, failing node, error, AI root cause, status) for one workflow_id. Use it to spot repeat failures.
Returns weekly Metrics_History snapshots (executions, failed, error_rate, p95_seconds, cost_usd) for one workflow_id. Use it as the normal baseline.

  "confidence": "High"
}
